summary: Source-anchored research for hasNextPage without computing total pages. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: For Relay connections, endCursor must be the cursor of the last node in edges and may be null only when there are no results, so it is non-null on a final nonempty page. Use hasNextPage for forward completion; if an implementation fetches an extra lookahead row and excludes it from edges, endCursor must be built from the last returned edge, not the discarded extra row (an inference from the spec's rule, not something the spec states about lookahead). Sources: https://relay.dev/graphql/connections.htm

Do not infer completion from a short or empty response when consuming an API. AIP-158 permits fewer than the requested number, including zero, before collection end; Samsara documents omitted inactive objects and instructs clients to continue while hasNextPage is true. (medium confidence) Sources: https://google.aip.dev/158 ; https://developers.samsara.com/docs/pagination

In the bounded matching-result pattern, receiving exactly pageSize rows cannot distinguish a full final page from a page with further results. Looking for the additional row resolves that boundary without calculating the total; this follows from Relay's strict greater-than-first condition and Spring's pageSize + 1 retrieval. (medium confidence) Sources: https://relay.dev/graphql/connections.htm ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spring-projects/spring-data-jpa/main/spring-data-jpa/src/main/java/org/springframework/data/jpa/repository/query/JpaQueryExecution.java

Lookahead removes the need for a count query: Spring's reference says a Page triggers a count query, while a Slice knows only whether a next Slice is available. MongoDB can coalesce a $limit into a preceding $sort so the sort maintains only the top n results; with an intervening $skip it increases the $limit value by the $skip amount. Sources: https://docs.spring.io/spring-data/jpa/reference/repositories/query-methods-details.html ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization/

A continuation token is not universally proof that another matching record exists. Google requires a token when the service cannot determine exhaustion in time, and DynamoDB explicitly says a nonempty LastEvaluatedKey does not necessarily mean more result data. Distinguish permission to continue scanning from an exact matching-row existence test. (medium confidence) Sources: https://google.aip.dev/158 ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/APIReference/API_Query.html

Avoiding a total-count query does not remove deep-offset costs. Spring documents that offset-based Slice queries become inefficient at large offsets and separately describes indexed keyset windows that fetch limit + 1 results. (low confidence)

Relay requires consistent edge ordering across pages. It also scopes hasNextPage by direction: first/after requires an exact further-edge answer, while last/before permits false when the server cannot efficiently determine whether later edges exist. (low confidence)

Use the cursor of the last returned edge as the next request's after value. If an implementation uses an extra-row probe, it should exclude the probe from edges and derive endCursor from the last displayed row, which the Relay spec's endCursor rule requires; the probe row then remains eligible for the next page. Sources: https://relay.dev/graphql/connections.htm

For forward pagination over an ordered stream of matching results, fetch pageSize + 1 results, return the first pageSize, and set hasNextPage to whether the extra result exists. This implements Relay's more-than-first test and Spring's documented Slice fetch size without needing a total-count query. (medium confidence) Sources: https://relay.dev/graphql/connections.htm ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spring-projects/spring-data-jpa/main/spring-data-jpa/src/main/java/org/springframework/data/jpa/repository/query/JpaQueryExecution.java ; https://docs.spring.io/spring-data/jpa/reference/repositories/query-methods-details.html

Continuation metadata can support forward navigation without total pages: Relay requires edges and pageInfo but does not require a total count, while Google AIP-158 makes total_size optional and communicates completion through next_page_token. (medium confidence) Sources: https://relay.dev/graphql/connections.htm ; https://google.aip.dev/158

Cursor pagination and hasNextPage suit sequential loading, but a cursor alone does not provide arbitrary page-number jumps or an exact total. Mironsoft describes both limitations and recommends matching the navigation model to the UI. (low confidence)

Incorrect continuation metadata can silently truncate client output. In an August 2022 GitHub GraphQL regression, a repository query returned hasNextPage=false despite further results; the reporter's generated profile lost project listings. A GitHub reply dated September 2, 2022 said the bug had been fixed about a week earlier. This is historical evidence, not a claim of a current defect. (low confidence)

Total counts are optional for forward traversal: a response can expose a next-page boolean or continuation token independently of total rows and total pages. Relay specifies pageInfo without requiring totals, Google makes total_size optional, and Spring distinguishes Slice from Page. (high confidence) Sources: https://relay.dev/graphql/connections.htm ; https://google.aip.dev/158 ; https://docs.spring.io/spring-data/jpa/reference/repositories/query-methods-details.html

A Next or Load more interface can use continuation metadata alone. A numbered last-page control needs additional information: Spring's Slice does not report total pages, while Google's pagination response permits omitting total_size. (medium confidence) Sources: https://docs.spring.io/spring-data/jpa/reference/repositories/query-methods-details.html ; https://google.aip.dev/158

Do not infer completion from a short or empty API response. Google permits zero results before collection exhaustion, Samsara documents empty pages with hasNextPage true, and DynamoDB can filter out every evaluated item while returning LastEvaluatedKey. Follow the API's continuation contract. (high confidence) Sources: https://google.aip.dev/158 ; https://developers.samsara.com/docs/pagination ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/APIReference/API_Query.html
